preamble: Each domain question draws from the complete medical record. Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost reflects typical test burden: Small = existing record / standard echo  |  Medium = targeted test or genetic panel ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = advanced imaging CT/MRI/RHC ($1,500–$5,000+)

questions.question: Is RV systolic pressure (RVSP) estimated >35 mmHg via peak TR jet velocity on Doppler (using Bernoulli equation)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — RVSP >35 mmHg is the primary echo screening criterion for pulmonary hypertension; velocity >3.4 m/s = intermediate-high probability per ESC/ERS guidelines

questions.question: Is the right ventricle dilated (RV:LV end-diastolic area ratio >1.0 on apical 4-chamber view)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — RV dilation reflects chronic pressure/volume overload from elevated PVR; RV:LV ratio >1.0 is a key severity marker

questions.question: Is there interventricular septal flattening or D-shaped LV on parasternal short axis echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — septal flattening with eccentricity index >1.0 indicates RV pressure or volume overload exceeding LV; D-shaped LV is a hallmark of significant PAH

questions.question: Is the main pulmonary artery diameter ≥25 mm on echo or CT (dilated PA)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — dilated PA is a marker of chronically elevated PA pressures; PA:aorta ratio >1.0 is an independent predictor of PAH

questions.question: Does right heart catheterization confirm mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) ≥20 mmHg at rest?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — mPAP ≥20 mmHg is the 2022 ESC/ERS updated hemodynamic threshold for pulmonary hypertension; replaces the older ≥25 mmHg criterion

questions.question: Is pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) ≥2 Wood units (WU) on RHC with normal PAWP (≤15 mmHg)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — PVR ≥2 WU + PAWP ≤15 mmHg confirms pre-capillary PAH and distinguishes it from left heart disease (Group 2 PH)

questions.question: Was vasoreactivity testing performed (inhaled NO or IV adenosine) and did the patient respond (mPAP decrease ≥10 mmHg to ≤40 mmHg)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — acute vasoreactivity response identifies the ~10% of idiopathic PAH patients who may respond to high-dose calcium channel blockers; critical for therapy selection

questions.question: Is NT-proBNP >300 pg/mL (or BNP >50 pg/mL) elevated at diagnosis or follow-up?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — NT-proBNP reflects RV wall stress; >300 pg/mL predicts worse outcomes and is a component of ESC/ERS risk stratification scoring

questions.question: Is uric acid elevated (>7 mg/dL) or is there evidence of systemic venous congestion (elevated creatinine, hepatic congestion on labs)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — elevated uric acid reflects tissue hypoxia and low cardiac output; hepatic/renal dysfunction indicates advanced RV failure and high-risk profile

questions.question: Are connective tissue disease antibodies (ANA, anti-Scl-70, anti-centromere, anti-SSA/SSB, anti-dsDNA) present on serologic workup?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — CTD-PAH (especially scleroderma-associated) is the most common associated form; serologic screening is mandatory at PAH diagnosis

questions.question: Has genetic testing identified a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in BMPR2 (most common), ALK1, ENG, SMAD9, CAV1, KCNK3, or ATP13A3?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — BMPR2 mutations account for ~70% of heritable PAH and ~15% of idiopathic PAH; confirms heritable PAH (HPAH) and enables cascade genetic screening of family members

questions.question: Is there a first-degree relative with confirmed PAH or known BMPR2/ALK1 pathogenic variant?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — family history of PAH carries ~10–20% lifetime penetrance for BMPR2 carriers; triggers mandatory surveillance echocardiography in carriers

questions.question: Is 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) <440 meters at baseline or declining on serial testing?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — 6MWD <440 m is an intermediate-risk marker per ESC/ERS PAH risk stratification; decline of >15% between visits predicts clinical worsening

questions.question: Is the patient in WHO functional class III or IV (symptomatic with mild exertion or at rest)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — WHO FC III/IV is an intermediate-to-high risk marker; FC II at diagnosis indicates earlier disease; FC guides treatment escalation decisions

questions.question: Is there a history of syncope or pre-syncope with exertion?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — exertional syncope in PAH reflects inability to augment cardiac output; associated with high mortality risk and triggers urgent therapy escalation

questions.question: Is the patient on combination PAH-targeted therapy (PDE5 inhibitor + ERA ± prostacyclin analog) with a low-risk profile at follow-up?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — achieving low-risk status (NT-proBNP <300 pg/mL, 6MWD >440 m, WHO FC I-II) on combination therapy is the treat-to-target goal per ESC/ERS 2022 guidelines

questions.question: Has sotatercept (Winrevair) been initiated for inadequate response to background oral therapy, with improvement in 6MWD or PVR?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — sotatercept (FDA approved March 2024) is the first activin signaling inhibitor for PAH; STELLAR trial showed 40.8-meter 6MWD improvement over placebo on background therapy

high.label: 🔴  80–100 High confidence
high.action: PAH confirmed or highly probable; initiate combination PAH therapy (ERA + PDE5i); refer to PAH center of excellence; risk stratify with ESC/ERS risk score; consider sotatercept for insufficient response

moderate.label: 🟡  50–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: RHC mandatory to confirm hemodynamics and PVR; complete PAH association workup (CTD serology, HIV, porto-pulmonary, genetic testing); echocardiographic follow-up in 3 months

low.label: 🟢  <50 Low confidence
low.action: insufficient evidence for PAH; investigate secondary causes (sleep apnea, CTEPH, LHD); consider exercise echo challenge if exertional dyspnea present; reassess with complete cardiopulmonary workup if symptoms progress
